01: The two arm segments form a hinge hierarchy of nested Groups (change rotation.z to pose it); open-ended ConeGeometry shade + emissive bulb + PointLight.
02: Assembled purely from Box/Cylinder; legs taper via cylinders with different top/bottom radii, the rear legs extend up to double as backrest posts, 5-slat backrest.
03: A single LatheGeometry profile makes the outer wall, thick rim, inner wall, and bottom in one go; the handle is a flattened half Torus.
04: 34 leaves arranged in a golden-angle (137.5°) spiral, growing larger, flatter, and shifting color from inside out — a textbook procedural-plant technique.
05: Fuselage Lathe profile generated from a sine function; fins are Shape + ExtrudeGeometry, copied three times at 120° around Y; the flame is an emissive cone.
06: Tower is 6 alternating red/white frustums; the base is Icosahedron rocks with randomly jittered vertices (seeded RNG, reproducible); emissive lantern room + point light.
07: Recursive branch() with 4 levels of forking, each cylinder segment oriented via quaternion; ends spawn flat low-poly foliage clusters. 237 meshes — the most "fragmented" of this batch.
08: A box() helper places blocks in bulk; arms are two-level shoulder→elbow Group joints, animatable. From batch 2 on, renders added environment lighting so metals no longer look black.
09: Wedge Shapes extruded into treads, 20 steps each turned 22.5°; the handrail is a CatmullRomCurve3 through the baluster tops, then TubeGeometry.
10: A piecewise teardrop function builds the Lathe profile, cut via phiStart/phiLength into 12 alternating-color "gores"; ropes use Line.
11: Arched cabinet = rectangle + semicircle Shape extruded with bevel; the cloth grille uses the same-shape ShapeGeometry, brass strips clipped to the arch by the circle equation; emissive dial.
12: Octagonal frustum tower (8-segment CylinderGeometry + flatShading); each of the four sails is a rotating Group with a spar, 8 crossbars, and translucent canvas.
13: Hand-written parametric hull surface: sine beam along length u, semicircle along section v, assembled directly into indexed BufferGeometry; the deck reuses the same profile function.
14: Body's figure-8 outline from two summed Gaussians, sound hole cut with Shape.holes; frets placed by 12-tone equal temperament 2^(-n/12) — real music theory here.
15: Side frames are all CatmullRomCurve3 + TubeGeometry sweeps, armrest ends parameterized into scrolls with decreasing radius; backrest slats placed along the curve.
16: 5 mushrooms share one mushroom(scale) function: Lathe stem + truncated-hemisphere cap + random white spots in spherical coordinates; moss is flattened low-poly spheres.
17: 12 merlons placed in a ring, rotated to face outward; arrow slits spiral up the tower; the arched door is an extruded Shape; the flag applies a sine displacement to PlaneGeometry vertices.
18: One bulbR(y) function drives both the glass and the sand pile at the bottom (Lathe); physically transmissive glass material; the three turned posts use |sin| for a beaded profile.
19: Subdivided Box vertices jittered to mimic crinkled gold foil; the parabolic dish is a Lathe of y=r²/4f directly, with the feed at the focus and struts aligned by quaternion.
20: Box built from 5 panels; the half-cylinder lid hangs on a rear-edge hinge Group opened about 110°; 170 gold coins share one geometry, heaped in a paraboloid and scattered on the ground. First render had the lid floating (wrong half of the cylinder); fixed.
21: Spokes are 24 thin cylinders placed by angle, alternating front/back; the frame uses a tube(a,b) helper to place a cylinder between any two points (quaternion-aligned), handlebars are a CatmullRom sweep; the basket uses a wireframe material to suggest weaving.
22: Body's top-view outline drawn as the curved rim with two Bézier segments, then extruded; 52 white keys, with the A–G pattern deciding where black keys go (36 in total). First render had the lid rotating down into the body (wrong direction); fixed.
23: Pot body is a Lathe of a semicircle parametric equation for an oblate sphere; the spout is TubeGeometry with vertices scaled ring by ring to taper — TubeGeometry doesn't support variable radius, so this is the usual workaround.
24: Body is a "rounded rectangle" Shape extruded in three layers (base plate/leather/top cover); the lens is a stack of coaxial cylinders, with 36 small blocks in a ring for the knurled focus ring.
25: Blades drawn flat as a Bézier Shape, then vertices twisted around the radial axis by x-coordinate to get propeller pitch; the guard's 24 spokes front and back bend along cosine arcs into spherical caps.
26: Bottle and glass are both Lathes; the glass wall gets thickness from a single curve of "outer profile + reversed inner profile"; the wine is the same bowl(y) function clipped at 45% height; the label is an open cylinder segment.
27: Anvil side profile (horn, face, waist) is one Shape extruded with bevel; stump vertices perturbed by sin(5a)+sin(11a) into an irregular cross-section, with growth rings on top.
28: Hydrant body is one Lathe from flange to dome; the pentagonal operating nut is simply a 5-segment CylinderGeometry; the three outlets share an outlet() function; the chain is small rings alternately rotated 90°.
29: Each of the 8 canopy panels is hand-written BufferGeometry: a concave height function + in-panel sin sag to mimic fabric stretched between ribs; ribs are tubes swept along the same height function; the J-shaped handle is a piecewise parametric curve.
30: 5 tiers, each shrinking by 0.84×; eaves are subdivided planes displaced by "pyramid slope + corner |xz|² upturn", so one function yields upturned eaves; a 9-ring spire on top.
31: Boiler, smokebox, and chimney (flared Lathe) arranged along x; the cowcatcher is an extruded triangle; 3 driving wheels + connecting rods on each side, two rails underneath.
32: Each sphere vertex gets a "terrain value" from a few summed low-frequency sines; above a threshold it's painted land, poles are white, written straight into vertexColors — a texture-free procedural Earth; tilted 23.5° overall.
33: Books generated in a "fill left to right" loop with random width/height/depth, about 8% leaning (rotated about the bottom corner, with the occupied width computed); the 126 materials are one color per book and could be merged.
34: The four candle arms are S-shaped CatmullRom tube sweeps, two high and two low; drip trays and flames are Lathes (the flame uses sin(π·t^0.6) for a droplet shape), with their own point lights.
35: Pentagonal wall Shape with a circular hole cuts the doorway directly; each roof slope has 5 rows of staggered shingles; a small bird made of spheres and a cone sits on the ridge.
36: Low-frequency noise on the snowball vertices makes them look "hand-packed"; the mouth is 7 coal pieces arced in spherical coordinates; the scarf is 12 alternating-color torus segments.
37: Tripod legs placed at 120° from foot to apex with quaternions; the tube sits in a tilted Group, with seg() stacking the dew shield, tube, and eyepiece; the finder scope hangs on a bracket.
38: Each of the 22 staves is an angular slice of LatheGeometry (phiStart/phiLength), with gaps and random shading; the barrel bulges via a parabolic radius, and hoop radii follow their height.
39: The 6 tube lengths follow base/√(frequency ratio) (1, 9/8, 5/4, 3/2, 5/3, 2) — a real acoustic relationship; strings use Line, and the central striker and wind sail hang on the same line.
40: Fuel tank, globe, and flame are all Lathes; the wire guard is swept along the globe profile pushed outward; the curved tubes on both sides mimic a hurricane lantern's air-intake frame, with its own point light.
41: The five-star base uses 5 rotated Groups reusing one component; the seat is a beveled rounded-rectangle extrusion; the backrest mesh is an open cylinder segment for a curved surface.
42: Helmet is a flat-topped Lathe stretched 1.08× in z for an elliptical cross-section; the cross reinforcement + rivets, eye slit, and 4×3 breathing holes are all placed on the surface in cylindrical coordinates; the plume is elongated low-poly spheres in a fan.
43: The C-shaped arm is an extruded curved Shape; three objectives of increasing length with colored magnification rings; first render had the objectives detached from the arm, fixed by adding a connector.
44: Paper cup is a Lathe with radius modulated by cos(36a) for pleats; the frosting is a conical spiral tube with rings scaled to a peak; 90 sprinkles share one Capsule geometry placed on the spiral surface.
45: Cones reuse a cone() function 3 times (one knocked over); reflective bands are short frustums matching the cone's slope; the barrier is striped from 8 red/white blocks.
46: The 5 piece types share a base profile, each attaching a different Lathe profile on top, then adding merlons, the bishop's cut, queen's crown beads, or king's cross by type — one piece(kind) function generates them all.
47: The tray is a hand-written BufferGeometry loft from "small bottom rectangle → large open rectangle"; the dirt pile is a flattened, perturbed hemisphere; the handles are tubes swept from the axle out under the tray.
48: Bell is a Lathe with a cos(16a) ruffled edge; oral arms are spiral tubes with sin-modulated radius for frills; 16 tentacles hang as sine waves with different phases, emissive + translucent.
49: Arched hood is an extruded rectangle + semicircle Shape; 60 dial ticks (hours bolder) placed by angle, hands set at 10:10; the pendulum and three weights are visible behind the glass door.
50: Twin wheel rims + 24 spokes + 12 crossbeams; 144 bulbs share one geometry; the 12 gondolas are added to root rather than the wheel so they always stay level. 264 meshes — the most complex of this batch.
51: One Lathe profile + dimples at both ends, plus a stem and a flattened sphere for the leaf. Only 3 meshes.
52: Dough is a flattened Torus; the glaze is a slightly larger Torus whose lower vertices are "flattened" onto a sin(9a) wave for a drippy edge; 70 sprinkles.
53: Oval tabletop = cylinder scaled 1.4×0.75; four tapered legs splay outward from under the table (cylinder between two points), with brass caps on the feet.
54: Built entirely from scaled spheres: body, head, beak, wings, and a cone for the tail. With a simple prompt, the model chose the most classic cartoon form.
55: A 6-sided cylinder is naturally a hexagonal pencil barrel; the sharpened wood and lead are two cones, with a metal ferrule + eraser at the other end.
56: Dial with 12 ticks + hour and minute hands; the two bells are hemispheres tilted outward with a small hammer between; the arched handle is half a Torus.
57: ribbed(r,h) function: a capsule with radius modulated by cos(8a) for ribs, then spines along each rib ridge; the trunk and both arms reuse it.
58: The 5×14 keyboard keys share one geometry; the screen uses vertexColors for a gradient wallpaper; the lid hangs on a rear-edge hinge Group, opened.
59: Double-cutaway body outline drawn with 6 Bézier segments; the sunburst color interpolates vertexColors by distance from center; frets by 12-tone equal temperament, with inlays at frets 3/5/7/9/12 (double)/15/17/19.
60: The external tank is an ogive Lathe, both boosters reuse srb(); orbiter fuselage + black heat-shield belly + double-delta wing + tail fin + 3 main engine nozzles.
61: Minimal prompt: a trunk + 12 low-poly spheres of random size and random green forming the canopy.
62: Box walls + extruded triangular roof + chimney, door, two windows, and sills. 92 triangles — among the leanest of all.
63: The model read "old key" as a skeleton key: ring bow + small trefoil rings + shaft + notched bit (extruded Shape).
64: The post uses cos(12a) modulation for fluting; the lamp head is a 4-sided frustum of glass + iron frame + pyramid cap, with its own point light.
65: An rbox() rounded-box function is reused 10 times for the base, back, arms, and cushions; the two throw pillows are flattened spheres.
66: The bowl is a spherical Lathe open at the top and flat at the bottom; the water reuses the same profile clipped at 70%; 60 pebbles, 5 water plants, 1 goldfish.
67: Clinker-built hull: each of the 6 strakes is hand-written BufferGeometry with 15% overlap; dragon-head prow + curled stern; striped sail via vertexColors; 9 shields and oars on each side.
68: A drum(r,depth) function makes the shell, both heads, hoops, and lugs, reused 6 times; the stand() tripod and cymbal() Lathe are reused too.
69: Tunnel-shaped mailbox = extruded rectangle + semicircle Shape, with the red flag raised on the side. 4 meshes.
70: The deck is an extruded rounded strip, then vertices displaced for kicktails along x and concave along y; two trucks + 4 colored wheels.
71: Ten points alternating between inner and outer radii draw the star Shape, extruded with bevel. The whole object is 1 mesh, 116 triangles.
72: Round brilliant cut profile (table, crown, girdle, pavilion) as a 16-segment Lathe, toNonIndexed + flatShading for facets, ior=2.4.
73: Open frustum pail body + bottom + 3 reinforcing ribs + bail handle.
74: Body side is an extruded rounded profile; two slices of toast pop out of the slots, with half-cylinders for the crust along the top edges; side lever and knob.
75: The headband is half a Torus stretched along z; ear cups are elliptical cylinders + cushion rings + gold logo; sliders and yokes are symmetric on both sides.
76: Tracks are an extruded "racetrack Shape with holes" + 18 grousers; upper body → boom → arm → bucket nested as Groups level by level; hydraulic cylinders use cyl() to place a barrel + chrome rod between two points.
77: 16 striped cone panels + scalloped valance + 48 bulbs; 8 horses generated by horse(), alternating high and low; the spiral brass poles are tubes swept along tight helices. 30k triangles — the heaviest of all.
78: Two sets of diagonal sin functions compute vertexColors on the cone for a diamond grid; the two scoops have slight noise undulation.
79: 5-plank tabletop, benches on both sides, A-frame legs with braces; the checked tablecloth is a subdivided plane with vertices beyond the edge folded down to hang.
80: The marble base uses summed sines for gray-veined vertexColors; the trophy is a single Lathe (base, knopped stem, cup), with S-shaped handles on both sides.
81: 7 spheres of different sizes + a flat cylinder base. 1 material.
82: Mushroom house: a bulging Lathe for the stem, cap edge curled inward, white spots fitted to the surface with lookAt; round door, glowing round window, chimney.
83: Upper and lower wings + ribs, interplane struts and cross-bracing wires, 7-cylinder radial engine, two-blade wooden prop, tail, spoked landing gear — implemented item by item from the prompt's list.
84: A single Lathe with a sine-bulged belly, vertexColors graded by height (celadon glaze to cream rim). 1 mesh.
85: Can body is a Lathe flattened in z; the long spout is a cone tube between two points; the rose has small holes in concentric circles; the handle spans the top.
86: Bridge body = extruded Shape with 3 semicircular holes; each arch ring extruded voussoir by voussoir; pier cutwaters, paving stones, parapets, and a stream. 172 materials (random shading per stone) — could be merged.
87: Beveled cubes + colored block "letters" on 5 faces, with 6 blocks stacked casually.
88: Machine side profile (pillar → arm → head) is one extruded curved Shape; gold decals are sine-swept tubes; handwheel, needle bar, presser foot, spool, and a line of stitching.
89: Classic bell-profile Lathe + thickened lip ring + crown loop on top + clapper.
90: The 4 triangular sail panels are BufferGeometry built directly from 3 points; cross spars; the tail is a wavy line with little bows. 76 triangles.
91: Shell = tube swept along a logarithmic spiral, each ring's radius shrunk by e^(-k·a), stripes via vertexColors. First render had the shell floating and eyes detached from the stalks; fixed.
92: Flat cylinder body + half-ring bumper + lidar turret + glowing button + three-prong side brush.
93: 28 wooden staves + 5 iron hoops + conical top; steel frame of four legs with cross bracing; ladder on the side.
94: 4 rows of staggered round keys (glass keycaps + chrome rings + key levers), 36 typebars in a fan; platen, knobs on both sides, a slightly curled sheet of paper, and the return lever. 200 meshes.
95: Snow blocks laid in hemispherical courses with staggered joints (half-block offset per row), skipping blocks at the entrance; half-cylinder tunnel + dark doorway.
96: Triangular Shape with a triangular hole cut for the doorway, then extruded; door flap rolled up; two guy ropes and stakes. 103 triangles.
97: Round-nosed, pointed-tail Lathe hull; the conning tower is a flattened capsule; bent periscope tube, 4 portholes per side, cross tail fins, 3-blade propeller.
98: Trunk + buttress roots + 6 main limbs (limb() places a cylinder between two points) + canopy clusters at the tips; platform, railing, little cabin with windows, shingled roof, rope ladder, tire swing.
99: Sphere pressed by |sin(5a)| into 10 pumpkin ribs, pulled in at the poles; hexagonal stem. 2 meshes.
100: The record uses concentric RingGeometry for grooves + a red label; tonearm and horn neck are swept tubes; the horn bell is an exponentially flared Lathe with a cos(8a) petal edge.
